clue.text: Scales tipped against popular government leader taking a rest

indicators.note: tipped over, the word for scales is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: scales are peels, the thin outer layers stripped off
in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: the leader of the word government is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Political cartoon: the balance has tipped against the popular head of government, who is having a lie-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scales' suggests a balance, as the surface wants, but here it means peels, the outer skins; 'against' only sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is resting, so the participle matches the phrase about having a rest.

clue.text: See 26 across
Mean to follow this middle course

definitions.text: Mean to follow this middle course

parts.words: Mean to follow this middle course
parts.note: the word that the word mean follows in the phrase naming the moderate path between extremes

explanation.surface: Advice to steer a moderate path between extremes.
explanation.walkthrough: The golden mean is the middle course between excess and deficiency, from Aristotle; the clue asks for the word that 'mean' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden mean is the classical name for moderation, the path between two extremes.

clue.text: No flyer needs oxygen, by the way — laughable!

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
ST is short for street, a way
rich, as in 'that's rich!', means laughable or absurd

explanation.surface: Someone who won't fly scoffs at the idea of needing an oxygen mask on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' and 'by' are link words joining the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is a large bird that cannot fly, hence a non-flyer.

clue.text: Like certain sisters said 'fruit'

indicators.note: said signals that the word is spoken, giving a word of matching sound

parts.note: the ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo

explanation.surface: Some sisters are being described with a word that sounds like a fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ugly Sisters are Cinderella's stepsisters in the British Christmas pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinderella's stepsisters in pantomime are always billed as the Ugly Sisters.

clue.text: Short time I'd arranged with ailing artist

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a brief time

indicators.note: arranged means these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ailing artist spends a brief moment putting his affairs in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ailing' reads as describing the artist but is part of the letters that 'arranged' scrambles; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amedeo Modigliani was an Italian painter and sculptor famed for elongated portraits.

clue.text: Corner the rest of Members of Parliament

definitions.meaning: a nook or corner in a wall

definitions.text: the rest of Members of Parliament
definitions.meaning: Parliament's ... is the break when Members are not sitting

explanation.definitionFit: A nook in a room and the holiday period when the legislature stops sitting share one name.

clue.text: Laid up in old island state

parts.note: someone laid up in bed is ill
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is laid up ill on an old island somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces simply follow in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Illinois is one of the fifty US states, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Could be a barnacle's inappropriate prod

definitions.meaning: the barnacle ... is a species, so a barnacle could be one
to poke them rudely in the bottom

explanation.surface: A shellfish giving someone an unwelcome poke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barnacle' looks like the shellfish but here is the barnacle goose.
explanation.definitionFit: The barnacle is a kind of wild bird, and the same word as a verb is a cheeky poke.

clue.text: Stupid person cutting end off sun-dried meat strips

indicators.note: the final letter is chopped off the word for dried meat

parts.note: jerky is meat cut in strips and dried

explanation.surface: A fool slicing the ends off strips of dried meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting end off' removes the last letter of JERKY.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerk is slang for a foolish or contemptible person.

clue.text: Scandalous secrets revealed to chambermaid

definitions.meaning: private scandal, as in washing it in public
a chambermaid sees the soiled bed sheets left in a room

explanation.definitionFit: Soiled sheets are literally what a hotel maid collects, and figuratively the scandal people hide.

clue.text: Robin playing over intro of boy band

indicators.note: the rearranged name goes over, covering, the single letter, so it sits around it
playing means the letters of the name are moved about into a new order
the intro of the word boy is its first letter

explanation.surface: Robin playing in a boy band, in front of the boy who introduces it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' turns ROBIN into RIBON, and 'over' sets it around B, the start of 'boy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon is a narrow band of fabric, such as one tied in hair.

clue.text: Uncommunicative book put out — end is awful

indicators.note: awful here means the letters are in a bad mess, needing reordering

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A book is withdrawn because its ending is terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges PUT OUT and END into UTTONEDUP; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone buttoned up is reserved and keeps their thoughts to themselves.

clue.text: Agent who changes players going round country with no capital

indicators.note: going round means the troupe of players surrounds the other piece

parts.note: the cast is the set of players in a show

indicators.note: the capital, or first letter, of the country's name is dropped

parts.note: Italy is a country

explanation.surface: An agent who changes the actors touring a country, but avoiding its capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like the country's chief city, but here it means its capital letter, the first one.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalyst is something or someone that brings about change, from chemistry's reaction-speeding agent.

clue.text: Salt content of tobacco

definitions.meaning: a salt is an old sailor
a residue found in tobacco smoke

explanation.definitionFit: Old seadog and the sticky residue in cigarettes share a three-letter word.

clue.text: A despicable person gets put away in stir

parts.note: git is British slang for a contemptible person
to put away food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: A villain gets locked up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' looks like slang for prison but is the verb; 'gets' and 'in' are link words. GIT is British slang for an unpleasant man.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate a liquid is to stir or shake it up.

clue.text: Bell's unfinished book

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word for a book is left off

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Someone named Bell has not finished writing their book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the last letter of TOME. Great Tom is the famous bell at Christ Church, Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Tom is a well-known bell, so a bell can be called Tom.

clue.text: The City Beautiful's light surrounded by gold ring

definitions.note: the definition with the possessive 's standing for 'is'

indicators.note: surrounded by means the first word sits within the pair of pieces that follow

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
O is ring-shaped
to light on something is to land on it

explanation.surface: A city's lighting is surrounded by a ring of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' is the verb, as in alight or settle, not illumination; 'surrounded by' places it between the gold and the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando in Florida has the long-standing nickname The City Beautiful.

clue.text: Avoid fish and small fowl

parts.note: to duck something is to dodge it
the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Instructions to avoid fish and also little birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A duckling is a young duck, a little bird of the poultry kind.

clue.text: Canned eels can have a purifying effect

indicators.note: canned is slang for drunk, so the following letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Tinned eels supposedly detox the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canned' looks like it describes the eels, but it means drunk and rearranges EELS CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse is to purify or clean thoroughly.

clue.text: Oddball sailor working over marines by a lake

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: over means the word for working is turned back to front

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: An eccentric sailor serving alongside marines beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns ON into NO; 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddball as an adjective means strange or unusual, so it fits abnormal.

clue.text: Cracker from a tube, possibly today's last

indicators.note: possibly means these letters could be arranged another way
the last of the word today's, ignoring the apostrophe, is its final letter

explanation.surface: A Christmas cracker pulled from a tube, perhaps the final one today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges A TUBE into BEAUT, then 'last' adds Y, the end of TODAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A cracker is informal for something excellent or a stunning person, just as a beauty is.

clue.text: Royal broadcast copies

indicators.note: broadcast signals the word is spoken out, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: prints are copies, as of a photograph

explanation.surface: A royal broadcast is copied and circulated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal' looks like an adjective describing the broadcast, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince is a member of a royal family, so a royal.

clue.text: Danish father's go?

parts.note: pa is father, and the possessive adds the S
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: A Danish dad taking his turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Danish' looks like a nationality but is the sweet bun.
explanation.definitionFit: A Danish is a sweet, flaky breakfast bun made of rich dough.

clue.text: Seabed and bank rocks that produce wind?

indicators.note: rocks means the letters are shaken about into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Geology: features of the seabed and riverbank that generate wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like geology but rearranges SEABED and BANK; 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Haricot beans in tomato sauce are notorious for causing flatulence.

clue.text: Honey bishop hid in tree

indicators.note: hid in means the abbreviation for the clergyman is tucked inside the tree

parts.note: the bay is the laurel tree
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop hides honey up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honey' looks like a food but is the term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey and baby are both affectionate terms for a sweetheart.

clue.text: Trips in central Kurdistan initially become unhealthy

parts.note: trips and falls are stumbles

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A traveller's trips into central Kurdistan make them ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' governs all of 'in central Kurdistan', giving I, C and K.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall sick is to become ill, an idiom for losing one's health.

clue.text: Bow adjuster changed for good

indicators.note: changed means the letters of the little word are put in another order

explanation.surface: A violinist's bow adjuster replaced permanently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns FOR into FRO; 'for good' looks like an idiom meaning forever.
explanation.definitionFit: The frog is the part at the heel of a violin bow, holding and tightening the hair.

clue.text: Area of Northumberland that's handy for suckers?

indicators.note: area of means an internal stretch of the long place name supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A region of an English county that suits gullible people.
explanation.walkthrough: Northumberland is England's northernmost county. 'handy' is a pun: a thumb is on the hand, and children suck it; 'that's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Children who suck their digit choose the one on the hand, so it is handy for them.

clue.text: Master knight called Hill

indicators.note: called means spoken aloud, so the title is given as it sounds

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir
a mount is a hill or mountain

explanation.surface: A master knight named Hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called' looks like it introduces a name but signals the sound of SIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a problem is to overcome or surmount it.
